question_text: Triangle ABC has $\mathrm{AB} = 8\text{ cm}$, $\mathrm{BC} = 10\text{ cm}$, and $\mathrm{AC} = 12\text{ cm}$.

subparts.stem: Draw a diagram clearly showing this information.

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct diagram of triangle ABC with sides 8 cm, 10 cm, 12 cm

subparts.solution: [Diagram of triangle ABC with side lengths AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm, AC = 12 cm]

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Construct a triangle labeled with given side lengths opposite their corresponding vertices.
step_by_step: Label side lengths: $AB = 8\text{ cm}$, $BC = 10\text{ cm}$, $AC = 12\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Mislabelling sides opposite the wrong vertices.

subparts.stem: Find the smallest angle in triangle ABC.

mark_breakdown.desc: Recognize that the smallest angle is opposite the shortest side AB
Use cosine rule to find cos(BCA)
Calculate angle BCA to obtain approximately 41.4°

subparts.solution:
The smallest angle in triangle ABC is opposite the shortest side.
$\therefore \text{B}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A}$ is the smallest angle.
By the cosine rule:
$$\cos\text{B}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A} = \frac{12^2 + 10^2 - 8^2}{2 \times 12 \times 10}$$
$$\therefore \cos\text{B}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A} = \frac{180}{240} = \frac{3}{4}$$
$$\therefore \text{B}\hat{\text{C}}\text{A} = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) \approx 41.4^{\circ}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In any triangle, the smallest angle is opposite the shortest side.
step_by_step: Compare sides: $AB = 8$, $BC = 10$, $AC = 12$. The shortest side is $AB = 8\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculating the angle opposite the longest side instead of the shortest.

subparts.stem: Find the area of triangle ABC.

mark_breakdown.desc: Use area formula Area = 1/2 * a * b * sin C with angle BCA
Evaluate area to obtain approximately 39.7 cm^2

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The area of a triangle given two sides and the included angle is $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
step_by_step: Use the two sides adjacent to angle $C$: $a = 10\text{ cm}$ and $b = 12\text{ cm}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the side opposite the angle in the $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ formula.
